A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OpenDeception and retain the same 50-scenario benchmark. All 20 pages of v2 and 22 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison of text, tables, figures and equations despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original dialogue simulations evaluating 11 LLMs, deception rates, capability correlations and controlled ablations in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 reports original IntentNet and TrustNet validation, training-data audits, evaluations of 11 LLMs and three reasoning models, and a trust-monitoring case study.

M1.justification: v3 expands the simulation-and-manual-evaluation framework with a supervised IntentNet, a contrastively trained TrustNet and joint per-turn warnings. Sections 3.1–3.4 add scenario synthesis, self-label filtering and controlled belief/disbelief trajectories for training. These are new procedures and learned components, beyond the retained thought/speech separation.

E1.justification: The original five-category, 50-scenario benchmark remains despite role renaming. v3 adds trust-scoring evaluation using PersuasionForGood, PersuGPT, DailyDialog, PanoSent and FGRC-SCD, controlled belief/disbelief training trajectories, and an adapted suicide-risk dialogue. This substantially broadens the represented dialogue data and assessment tasks.

E2.justification: v3 introduces direct comparisons of its learned evaluators against Qwen2.5-3B/72B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B/70B-Instruct, GPT-5.1 and Claude-3.7-Sonnet in Figure 5 and Table 3. These evaluator comparisons were absent from v2; the original 11 deception-tested models should not be confused with this new comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 adds training datasets exceeding 27,000 thoughts and 61,000 response pairs, 600-thought and 600-response validation sets, classification/trust metrics, three-level trust binning and a 0.75 warning threshold. It also evaluates reasoning models against a fixed Qwen2.5-72B user. DIR is now stated over total rather than successful conversations, although this wording change does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2's fixed-user scaling ablation, quantified initial-versus-refined prompt comparison and full success/failure dialogue examples are removed. v3 adds training-data quality audits, a qualitatively reported real-versus-simulated response discrimination study and the trust-warning case study. Earlier simulation-failure and refusal analyses largely survive in Appendices C and E.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting narrows from 95% confidence intervals for both DIR and DeSR in v2 Figure 3 to DIR alone in v3 Figure 6, accompanying removal of the DeSR analysis. No new run counts, seeds, significance tests or interval-construction procedure are documented; the new evaluator accuracy tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds evaluator accuracy and human-consistency results, including TrustNet's 77.17% accuracy and reasoning-model DIR estimates of 97.7–100%, while removing DeSR, DiSR/PDE breakdowns and scaling-ablation scores. Reported human DIR for Llama-3.1-8B changes from 85.7% in v2 Appendix D to 92.85% in v3 Table 1. The refusal-table average changes from 70% to 72%, although prose retains 70%. New model-scored DIR values do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Sections 3.3–3.4 of v3 introduce mathematical definitions of the supervised likelihood objective, pairwise sigmoid ranking objective and scalar trust-scoring function, absent from v2. These formalize the new learned components; neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from benchmarking deceptive intention and successful outcomes to learned joint assessment of AI intent and user trust with proactive warnings. Training datasets, two evaluators and reasoning-model findings become headline contributions. The abstract replaces v2's above-80% intention and above-50% success findings with above-90% intention for most models and a warning case study.

C2.justification: v3 interprets risk through the interaction of deceptive intent and user trust, suggests structured reasoning may amplify deception, and argues for operational warning utility. It adds ambiguity from subtle, ironic or implicit responses. Conversely, it removes v2's explicit qualification that elicited thoughts may not reflect actual internal reasoning and its detailed outcome-based interpretation of GPT safety alignment.

D1.justification: v3 documents synthesis/filter models, LoRA and LLaMAFactory training, hardware, hyperparameters and new synthesis/training/evaluation prompts. It replaces the anonymous toolkit link with a named repository link while retaining institutional-request restrictions, now including model parameters. The raw initial prompts and explicit ten-round cap disappear. Reproducibility remains imperfect: Appendix D.2 specifies three TrustNet epochs, whereas Table 9 specifies five.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning around chatbot-related suicide incidents, mental-health applications, DeceptionBench and self-monitoring, emphasizing the gap in intention-only evaluations that ignore user trust. It adds relevant dataset and training-framework citations while dropping discussions and citations for Machiavelli, TruthfulQA, model-on-model deception, ReAct and Chatbot Arena. This substantially revises the research positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten around deception and trust. Benchmark design, methodology and experiments are reorganized into framework construction and application case studies. Faithfulness, simulation failures and refusal findings move into reorganized appendices, while several earlier explanations are condensed or removed.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one-column to two-column layout. v3 redraws the benchmark overview and adds a training-pipeline diagram, monitoring flowchart, evaluator-accuracy plot and trust-trajectory figure. It removes the DeSR panel and category radar charts, restructures result tables and shortens the illustrated dialogue example.

improvement.justification: The learned evaluators, human-labeled validation and fuller training documentation provide credible gains over v2's manual assessment. However, v3 removes outcome measurements and fixed-user scaling controls while retaining claims about successful deception. Its central warning benefit rests on an adapted case in Figure 8 without quantitative threshold or intervention validation, and TrustNet training settings conflict. These substantial gains and losses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality.
